# Verañjaka Sutta (MN 42 (PTS MN i 290))

**ID:** MN 42 (PTS MN i 290)

**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Verañjaka Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 290
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Verañjaka Sutta* ("Discourse to the Verañjakas" or "The People of Verañja", MN 42) is the forty-second text of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Buswell & Lopez 2014]. The discourse was delivered at Sāvatthi when a group of Brahmin householders (*brāhmaṇagahapatikā*) from Verañja arrived on business and visited the Buddha [Hazra 1994; McTighe; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Functioning essentially as a repetition of the preceding *Sāleyyaka Sutta* (MN 41), the sutta expounds the moral conduct leading to rebirth in fortunate or unfortunate destinations [Humphreys 1956; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. The Buddha details ten unwholesome and ten wholesome courses of action, categorizing them into three bodily misdeeds (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct), four verbal misdeeds (falsehood, malicious gossip, harsh speech, and frivolous talk), and mental actions, demonstrating how virtuous practice yields happiness, auspicious rebirths, or birth according to one's aspiration [Hazra 1994; Rogell 2003; Buswell & Lopez 2014].
